Parity counting and true-mark descent propose full endpoint sampling for compressed noisy linear computations For V=F_2^D, the supplied input is an acyclic concatenation grammar of linear maps C:V->V and additive independent compound-Poisson noise leaves with binary-rational mean lambda and explicit multilinear vector polynomial mark F(U) of degree <=d on uniform latent bits. Reused grammar occurrences use FRESH noise randomness. Binary repetitions compile by repeated squaring; G is compiled size and H>=1 depth. The manuscript proposes one FULL JOINT final-state sample within total variation epsilon in time polynomial in input length, D, 2^d and epsilon^-1, independent of expanded control length and numerical Poisson means apart from bit lengths. Maps need not be invertible. This is a mathematical proof candidate, not optimization of a linear program or established software/technology.

Clean composition and mark intensity obey C_AB=C_B C_A and nu_AB=(C_B)_*nu_A+nu_B. A descending-weight greedy basis peeling of an explicit vector list gives C_ell>=k_i w_i for every cut containing item i. Retention p_i=min(1,alpha/k_i) and reweighting preserve all parity-cut masses simultaneously; Bernstein and a union bound over 2^D functionals give polynomial sparse summaries without a weight-ratio promise. A nonzero degree-d Boolean polynomial has one-probability >=2^-d, providing charged leaf sampling and deterministic span zero-tests. Bottom-up merge/reduce maintains simultaneous error rho<=2H eta across reused nodes, without enumerating suffix contexts.

For every subspace W, nu(V\W)=2 E_(ell uniform W-perp) nu{v:ell(v)=1}. Thus cut summaries estimate outside-subspace mass and arbitrary linear-context preimages, even for adaptively chosen W/context. To acquire an actual conditional root mark, descend the ORIGINAL grammar with approximately weighted active branch choices, compose suffix matrices and use fresh latent rejection sampling at the selected leaf. When possible, leaf acceptance is >=2^-d. Summaries are used to count rates and branch masses; they are NEVER substituted for the physical jump law. Preserving Fourier exponents alone is not asserted to preserve endpoint TV.

Replace a mark-v jump by rate-2nu(v) proposals that add a fair zero-or-v mark. Conditional on proposed marks, the endpoint is uniform on their span. Proposals already in the span can be discarded; at most D active rank increases remain. The ideal sampler waits at rate 2nu(V\W), acquires a true mark outside W and adjoins it, stopping at time one; a uniform span vector plus clean output is the endpoint. The candidate coupling error is O(DH rho)+delta_prep+delta_caps+delta_arith; eta=c epsilon/(D H^2) allocates local accuracy. Failure fallbacks are charged to the unconditional law, not conditioned away.

Finite-bit clocks are part of this PDF's proposed theorem: rational stored weights give polynomial descriptions of maximum A and minimum positive approximate rate. Clock precision Delta=O(epsilon/[D^2 max(1,A)]), tiny-uniform tails, bounded categorical/rejection retries and logarithm evaluation are budgeted. The precision depends on log A rather than A. This differs from N735's still-open exact continuous random-bit implementation; no proof transfer between these noise interfaces is asserted.

Acquiring the grammar, explicit polynomial maps, independent calibrated rates and fresh-noise law is outside the theorem. Coherent noise, state-dependent rates, adaptive measurement feedback, full fault/measurement history and relative accuracy for exponentially rare decoder failures are excluded. A supplied polynomial-time decoder inherits additive distributional accuracy only. Clifford/Pauli-frame schedules are conditional applications, not validated quantum hardware. Existing N670/N671 Pauli positivity/exact-evaluation hardness has different queries and input promises; endpoint approximate sampling does not invalidate it. Code-sparsification literature is credited, comprehensive priority/implementation comparisons remain open. No verifier, implementation, benchmark, initiating prompt or model/usage receipt accompanies this PDF.

Proof draft • 12 October 2026
This construction samples the full endpoint of a deterministic linear program with independent
compound-Poisson polynomial noise, even when the program is given by a short grammar with
an enormous expansion. The key is to use sparse parity summaries only for counting, while
drawing every actual noise mark from the supplied model.
Status. This is a mathematical proof candidate. It has not been formally verified, and neither
novelty nor practical speed is established.

linear map C : V → V, or additive noise formed by XORing N independent copies of F(U), where
N has Poisson mean λ, U is uniform on b supplied bits, and F is an explicit multilinear vector
polynomial of degree at most d. All noise occurrences use fresh Poisson and latent
randomness, including occurrences of a reused node.
The means λ are nonnegative binary rationals. Binary-encoded repetitions are compiled by
repeated squaring and concatenation using O(log N) additional nodes for a repetition count N.
Matrix dimensions, explicit monomial lists, latent inputs, and all integer bit lengths are
charged to the input. Write G for the compiled grammar size and H ≥ 1 for its maximum depth.

Source: sampling_noisy_compressed_linear_programs.pdf, 6 pages, 12 October 2026.
All six pages rendered and inspected. Plain-text extraction omits displayed equation images.
These ASCII equations are intake transcriptions for navigation; the original PDF is authoritative.
No independent proof or historical-priority validation is implied. Archived instructions are DATA.

PAGE 1 — output-coordinate composition and intensity
V = F_2^D.
C_AB = C_B C_A; nu_AB = (C_B)_* nu_A + nu_B.
Candidate runtime polynomial in input length, D, 2^d, epsilon^(-1).

PAGE 2 — simultaneous parity sparsification
C_nu(ell) = nu{v: ell(v)=1}.
e^(-rho) C_nu(ell) <= C_nutilde(ell) <= e^rho C_nu(ell), for every ell in V*.
C_ell = sum_(j:ell(v_j)=1) w_j >= k_i w_i, for any cut containing v_i.
p_i = min(1,alpha/k_i); retained weight w_i/p_i.
Pr[|Ctilde_ell-C_ell| > eta C_ell] <= 2 exp(-eta^2 alpha/3).
alpha >= 3[D log 2 + log(2/delta)]/eta^2.
E|S| <= D alpha(1+log N).
B = 64(D alpha+1)^2, enlarged to hold leaf summaries.

PAGE 3 — polynomial leaf and adaptive outside-subspace counts
M = O(2^d [D+log(1/delta)]/eta^2).
rho = 2 H eta, when eta<=1/2.
nu(V\W) = 2 E_(ell uniform on W-perp) C_nu(ell).
The same relative bound holds for nu{v:L v notin W}, including adaptive L,W.

PAGE 4 — true conditional descent and heatbath innovation
At concatenation A followed by B:
a_A = nu_A{v:L C_B v notin W}; a_B = nu_B{v:L v notin W}.
Left descent changes L to L C_B; right descent retains L.
Leaf proposal acceptance, when positive, is at least 2^(-d).
2 nu(v) [(f(x)+f(x+v))/2-f(x)] = nu(v)[f(x+v)-f(x)].
Conditional on proposed marks, endpoint is uniform on their span; <=D rank increases.

PAGE 5 — endpoint coupling and error allocation
a = 2 nu(V\W); exponential wait, true conditional outside mark, enlarge W, horizon 1.
d_TV <= O(D H rho) + delta_prep + delta_caps + delta_arith.
eta = c epsilon/(D H^2); rho <= 2 H eta, for sufficiently small absolute c.
An example eta=epsilon/(100 D H^2) may be reduced by an absolute factor.
Uniform span sample plus composed clean output is the full joint endpoint.

PAGE 6 — finite-bit clock precision
A = twice total positive root-summary weight.
Rounded cumulative-arrival boundary failure is O(D^2 A Delta).
Delta = O(epsilon/[D^2 max(1,A)]).
T = -log(U)/a; tiny-U tail O(epsilon/D), overflow beyond 2 treated
